title: the cairn device publishes a proof's bus of its own
intention: Proofs outside the cairn device that need a bus of their own (a real store, nobody live listening) import the bus machine's code directly; the cairn device publishes a scratch_bus tool, BusDevice.scratch and the BusShim constructor behind published_by_device, so they reach it through its public interface.
why: Measured 2026-11-11: the build inspector run filed inspector-new-finding-encapsulation-holds naming seven sites in cairn/devices/codemother/proofs/test_charter_held.py:51-52, test_codemother.py:749, cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_a_hollow_seal_is_announced.py:40, test_the_seal_announces_itself.py:45 and test_the_tester_takes_its_reply.py:45-46, each importing cairn.devices.cairn.machines.bus.bus or .shim. Their teeth need a bus of their own: a fixture seal live codemother must not hear, a store flush writes and undelivered reads, codemother genuinely unwired. The live bus over bus_client.reach (12e6ecd87700's route) gives none of the three.
traces_to: CLAUDE.md RULE 1; outline 2.3.7.1 (a device's public interface is the bus plus any tool it publishes); outline 17.13.1.
how: New tool cairn/devices/cairn/tools/scratch_bus/: scratch_bus.py with scratch_bus(prefix, device_id) (a context manager over BusDevice.scratch) and bus_shim(bus, heartbeat) (the BusShim constructor); its charter says published_by_device true and names the one module. New proof proofs/test_a_proof_gets_a_bus_of_its_own.py, one tooth per clause. The five consuming proofs move in their own tickets, one per device.
